speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the appearance of the rash on your scalp and forehead? Is it itchy, painful, or scaly?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. Given your father's history of psoriasis and the rash appearing worse in cold weather, could you tell me if there are any silver-colored scales or if the rash has spread to the elbows or knees? Also, has the baby been diagnosed with any other conditions like eczema?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cradle Cap (Seborrheic Dermatitis)

I have noted the presence of greasy yellow scales, which is the hallmark of this condition. Please proceed with the care instructions for managing the scales and the redness.
